findings.claim: The sidecar text rewrite breaks the copy's own hash check. Every .abstract.md/.overview.md copied from blog-scraper (outside the 26 shared keys) is rewritten by cat|sed|rcat, so its hash no longer matches the old object. `rclone check --one-way` on blog-scraper skips only the 26 shared keys, so it reports every rewritten sidecar as differing and the job exits non-zero. The outcome ("job exits 0, so every old file ... at its key with the same hash") cannot hold for those keys. The plan must say how the rewritten sidecars are checked instead (for example: excluded from the hash check, then checked for presence and for holding no `blog-scraper/` URI), and the outcome must stop promising the same hash for them. The same goes for re-runs: the rewrite step needs the same skip-existing rule as the copy.

vectors_only likely leaves image files unindexed, and no spike covered them. The four trees hold 71 non-text files (clips 40 png + 1 jpg of 182 files, blog-scraper 25 webp, 4 png, 1 gif). In v0.4.17.1-9, `ReindexExecutor._best_resource_file_vector_text` embeds content only for TEXT types; for an image it uses the summary from `_best_file_summary`, which parses only `## <filename>` H2 sections of the parent .overview.md, while the real overview prompt (`prompts/templates/semantic/overview_generation.yaml`) writes one H3 link per entry. With a fresh schema there is no existing L2 record to fall back on, so the image is counted `unsupported` ("No vector source found"), not `failed`. The re-index would report failed 0 while the images are dropped from search, and the outcome's 10-random-files title search on clips (about 1 in 4 files is an image) would likely miss. Spikes 1 and 3 used .md files only and a stub VLM that writes `## Entries`. Next step is a spike: after a key-for-key copy of a directory holding a .png with sidecars in the real overview format, does vectors_only write an L2 row for the image and does find return it? If not, the plan needs a path for image directories (semantic reindex there, or an operator acceptance that images are not searchable) and an outcome that counts `unsupported`.

The sidecar rewrite broke the hash check. The plan now leaves rewritten blog-scraper sidecars (and the 26 shared keys) out of the hash check, checks them on their own (each present at its blogs/ key, no blog-scraper/ text under blogs/), and gives the rewrite skip-existing semantics.

Images got no vector after vectors_only. spike:ov-carry-over/4 shows no re-index mode fixes it in 0.4.17.1 and that copying the old level-2 row (INSERT ... SELECT, no VLM call) makes find return the image and survives a later vectors_only. The plan copies the 52 old rows after the re-index and checks each one.

The plan promises that 'nomad job dispatch ov-carry-over re-runs it, and a re-run only adds missing keys', but only the blog-scraper copy uses --ignore-existing. clips, leo and blogs copy with plain rclone copy, which overwrites any target whose hash differs. After step 3 the merged blogs/ and blogs/<source>/ sidecars are regenerated on purpose, and once the instance is live, ov-clip and the blog scraper add files that make OpenViking rewrite parent .overview.md/.abstract.md under clips/ and blogs/. A re-run then puts the old sidecars back over the new ones without a word, and the 'rclone check --one-way' hash check fails on exactly those keys, so the re-run cannot exit 0 either. Fix: make every copy skip existing keys, and define what the hash check means once the target's sidecars have moved on. For example, on every run check only that non-sidecar files are present with the same hash, and that sidecars are present.
Rewritten blog-scraper sidecars are out of the hash check and checked on their own.
Old image rows are copied into the new schema after the re-index, as spike:ov-carry-over/4 tested.
Every copy and the rewrite skip existing keys, and the hash check covers only non-sidecar, non-shared files, so a re-run neither overwrites regenerated sidecars nor fails its own check.

Main's ov-save-skill (ADR 0023) writes viking://user/jasper/resources/.map.md on Hermes's first save. fs/ls with show_all_hidden lists it, so after the merge the script's 'nothing else' check fails with 'unexpected top-level entry .map.md' unless the operator guesses --allow .map.md. The how-to only says to pass --allow for 'a name you created on purpose', which an operator who never made .map.md by hand will not read as covering it. Either accept .map.md by default in compare() (it is a known writer now, and the test already treats it as allowed) or name it in step 4 of the how-to.

entries.change: The "nothing else" check accepts the save skill's .map.md under resources/ by default, so the run after ov-save-skill needs no --allow.
The comparison test passes no allowed names, so it proves .map.md is accepted by default.

findings.claim: the outcome check rejects the save skill's top-level .map.md (ADR 0023) by default
